messages:
incident-bot: PAGE (P2) — continuous-batching runtime high tail latency on prod clusters (gpu-pool-3). Alert: gpu_util > 95% for 6m, tail_latency_95 > 2s. playbook: https://internal.playbooks/redwood/cont-batch

alice: oncall alice here, ack. paging SREs @bob @priya. checking traffic shape and recent deploys.

bob: looking at metrics — many tiny requests (mean tokens 8) causing poor packing; GPU overhead high from many small batches. logs from batch-controller: ```WARN packer: created 124 batches in 60s; median batch_size=3; tail_batch_latency=2200ms```

priya: not seeing recent deploys that would cause this. hypothesis: sudden spike of low-priority streaming chat from partner sandbox. customer-ops @carlos any reports?

carlos: confirmed — two customers (acme-inc, beta-sandbox) report errors on /v1/generate and /v1/embeds. Error is 503 or long hangs. ACME on enterprise tier, they care about availability. Beta-sandbox traffic is chatty and low priority.

bob: immediate options: (A) shed low-priority traffic via rate-limiter quotas, (B) increase continuous-batching window / max_batch to improve GPU throughput (will increase P50/P95 latencies), (C) reduce packing overhead by disabling streaming on some routes, (D) fallback to smaller model for free-tier. We should do a combination to restore headroom quickly.

priya: propose timeline: 1) apply rate-limit on free/beta tenants to 5rps for generate/embed routes; 2) increase continuous_batch.window_ms from 25 -> 75 and max_batch_items from 64 -> 256 on canary hosts; 3) disable chunked streaming for /v1/generate on free tier for 30m. Test canary for 5 minutes then ramp.

alice: +1. prioritize keeping enterprise traffic available. diana — product ok with temporary degradation of latency for non-enterprise users?

diana: ok to proceed. notify customers if any enterprise is impacted; otherwise we prefer availability over low-latency for sandbox.

bob: executing step 1 (rate limits). command: ```rictl rate-limit update --route /v1/generate --selector tier:free,beta-sandbox --rps 5 --burst 10 --reason "live-mitigation: GPU saturation"```

bob: rate limits applied to selectors. immediate qps drop ~28% on packer input. monitoring...

priya: applying canary config to continuous-batching controller: ```rictl set-config continuous_batch.window_ms=75 continuous_batch.max_batch_items=256 --service cont-batching --env prod --hosts canary-1,canary-2```

priya: canary deployed. logs: ```INFO cont-batch: window_ms=75 max_items=256 packer: median_batch_size=18 tail_batch_latency=600ms gpu_util=72%```

alice: good signal. now promote to 50% traffic. command: ```rictl traffic-shift cont-batching --from=baseline --to=variant-canary --percent=50 --duration=2m```

bob: promoting. also disabling streaming on free tier: ```rictl feature-toggle set streaming=false --route /v1/generate --selector tier:free,beta-sandbox --duration 30m```

bob: streaming disabled for free tiers. combined effect: input qps down 40% for packer, GPU util reduced to ~68%, request error rate dropped under 0.5% for enterprise routes.

carlos: ACME support: they confirm reduced errors and resumed traffic. will send brief note that we are doing mitigations and may increase latency for sandbox users.

priya: plan for next 30m: keep canary variant, observe model quality and latencies; if stable, promote config to all hosts. open follow-ups: (a) investigate root cause of sudden small-request spike, (b) consider long-term change: autotune window_ms based on request size distribution, (c) add tenant-aware packing to avoid penalizing enterprise traffic.

alice: agreed. I'll keep monitoring and will page if any regressions. added runbook note: "live-mitigation 3187654321: increased batch window, applied rate limits to free tiers, disabled streaming for free tier".

diana: thumbs up. please post postmortem if root cause is not just benign traffic test.

bob: capturing metrics snapshot and will drop into incident tracker. closing initial mitigation phase.

incident-bot: note: mitigation actions logged to incident-3187654321. Next check-in scheduled +15m.
